primary_work.author: J. Peter May
primary_work.title: The Cohomology of Restricted Lie Algebras and of Hopf Algebras; Application to the Steenrod Algebra
identity_locators: PDF page 2: full title and author
PDF page 3: Princeton dissertation accepted May 1964
primary_work.plain_text_note: The primary PDF is scanned. The available text extraction does not contain the mathematical body; no usable full-text extraction is claimed.

may_lowDimensionalProducts_permanent.locator: Paragraph after Remarks II.7.2: multiplication by h0 on E-infinity corresponds to multiplication by 2.

Theorem II.7.9(3),(4),(13), followed by the paragraph identifying the right-hand classes as E-infinity survivors: nu corresponds to h2 (order 8), sigma to h3 (order 16), nu-star to h2 h4 (order 8). This gives h0 h2, h0 h3, h2 h4 nonzero survival.

may_lowDimensionalSquares_permanent.locator: The zero stable stem is Z and h0 acts as multiplication by 2; this supplies the j=0 h0-square case.
Theorem II.7.9(2): pi(1)=Z/2 generated by eta and pi(2)=Z/2 generated by eta-square; eta corresponds to h1.
Theorem II.7.9(3),(4),(9), followed by the E-infinity-survivor identification: nu corresponds to h2 and nu-square generates pi(6); sigma corresponds to h3 and sigma-square is nonzero in pi(14).

retained_article_1966.title: The cohomology of restricted Lie algebras and of Hopf algebras
retained_article_1966.relationship: The article is a revision of part of the doctoral thesis (printed page 123, footnote 2). Its introduction (printed page 124) redirects stable-homotopy applications to other work; it is not the Part II Section 7 source for these two fields.

metadata_scope.openalex.json: Retained raw acquisition metadata for the 1966 Journal of Algebra article, not metadata for the primary 1964 thesis.
metadata_scope.source-status-1966.json: Unmodified original source-status acquisition record, preserved to make the earlier bibliographic mismatch auditable.
metadata_scope.article-1966.citation.bib: Unmodified original citation.bib; its historical Maythesis key denotes the 1966 article and is not the current canonical binding.

correction_note: The former Maythesis DOI and article-only citation were incorrectly used for thesis Part II stable-stem results. The canonical citation and paper.pdf now identify the 1964 thesis; the 1966 article and raw historical metadata are retained separately. Acquisition and hash checks do not establish formal proof completion.
